title: Radiologist
description: Company Description The hiring organization is a healthcare provider committed to delivering high-quality diagnostic and clinical services to the local community in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The facility is focused on expanding access to advanced medical imaging and radiology services to support accurate diagnosis and treatment. Team members collaborate across disciplines to provide safe, patient-centered care grounded in evidence-based practices. The organization values professional growth, ethical standards, and continuous improvement in clinical outcomes. Radiology professionals joining the team can expect a supportive environment that encourages learning and excellence in practice. Role Description This is a full-time, on-site Radiologist role based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The Radiologist will interpret a wide range of diagnostic imaging studies, such as X-rays, CT scans, MRI, ultrasound, and mammography, and provide clear, timely reports to referring clinicians. Day-to-day responsibilities include reviewing patient histories, selecting appropriate imaging protocols, ensuring image quality, and correlating imaging findings with clinical information. The Radiologist will participate in multidisciplinary discussions, communicate results and recommendations to healthcare teams, and contribute to patient counseling when needed. Additional tasks may include supervising radiologic technologists, supporting quality assurance initiatives, adhering to radiation safety standards, and engaging in continuing education to maintain up-to-date clinical knowledge. Qualifications Strong foundation in Medicine, including comprehensive clinical knowledge and patient-centered care. Proficiency in Radiology and Medical Imaging, with experience interpreting common modalities (e.g., X-ray, CT, MRI, ultrasound). Experience or training in Nuclear Medicine, including safe use of radiopharmaceuticals and interpretation of functional imaging. Competence in Mammography, with skills in screening, diagnostic imaging, and appropriate follow-up recommendations. Recognized medical degree and completed residency or specialist training in Radiology (or equivalent credential). Valid medical license or eligibility for licensure in Ethiopia, and compliance with local regulatory requirements. Attention to detail, strong analytical and diagnostic skills, and ability to produce clear, concise reports. Effective communication skills and ability to work collaboratively with multidisciplinary healthcare teams. Commitment to patient safety, radiation protection principles, and continuous professional development.

title: Pattern Maker
description: Company Description Sunshine Ethiopia Wool Textile is a growing textile manufacturer specializing in wool and related fabric products for local and international markets. The company focuses on quality craftsmanship, reliable production processes, and timely delivery to meet the needs of fashion brands and garment manufacturers. Working with modern machinery and skilled professionals, Sunshine Ethiopia Wool Textile aims to create durable, well-designed textiles that support a range of apparel styles. Team members are encouraged to contribute their technical expertise and creativity to continuously improve products and processes. Role Description The Pattern Maker role at Sunshine Ethiopia Wool Textile is a full-time, on-site position based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The Pattern Maker will translate design concepts and technical specifications into accurate patterns for wool and mixed-fabric garments, ensuring proper fit and production efficiency. Daily tasks include drafting and adjusting patterns, collaborating with designers and sample makers, and overseeing fittings to confirm size, shape, and garment structure. The role involves working closely with sewing and cutting teams, using both manual techniques and computer-aided design tools, and maintaining clear documentation for production. The Pattern Maker is expected to support continuous improvement in pattern quality, minimize material waste, and help meet production timelines. Qualifications Candidates should possess strong Pattern Making and Pattern Design skills, with the ability to create and modify patterns for various garment types. Candidates should possess practical Sewing and Fitting skills to evaluate prototypes and ensure garments meet design and comfort requirements. Candidates should possess experience with Computer-Aided Design (CAD) tools for pattern development, grading, and technical documentation. Candidates should possess strong attention to detail, measurement accuracy, and the ability to interpret technical drawings and specifications. Candidates should possess effective communication and teamwork skills to collaborate with designers, production staff, and quality control teams. Relevant vocational training or a diploma in textile, fashion design, garment technology, or a related field is beneficial. Prior experience as a Pattern Maker or in garment manufacturing is preferred, especially within wool or heavy fabric production.

description:

This role coordinates and provides technical input into the design and implementation of monitoring and evaluation (M&E) frameworks, supports learning processes, and provides technical advice to teams and Network Members. Organisational Performance and Monitoring and Evaluation Frameworks Coordinate and provide technical input into the development and implementation of robust M&E frameworks and tools for global programmes, advocacy initiatives, and Impact Vehicles. Support Impact Vehicle, cross-functional, and programmes teams in defining indicators, setting baselines, and tracking outcomes aligned to HelpAge’s Global Impact Framework. Coordinate the development and review of results frameworks, log frames, indicators, baselines, and targets across teams and Impact Vehicles. Lead the identification and development of appropriate data sources, data-collection methodologies and evidence requirements for organisational and Impact Vehicle indicators and targets. Act as the organisational focal point for standardising KPI measurement across all Impact Vehicles, establishing and maintaining consistent indicator definitions, measurement tools, evidence requirements and reporting approaches, subject to final technical sign-off by the Global Impact Adviser. Coordinate organisation-wide Impact Vehicle performance tracking, working with relevant teams to ensure the timely and consistent collection, analysis and reporting of results. Coordinate and undertake the drafting and revision of organisational MEAL policies, procedures, standards and guidance. 2. Technical MEL Support for Global Impact Team Provide advanced technical MEAL advice, support, and quality assurance across HelpAge’s global programme portfolio, working with programme teams and Network Members throughout proposal development, programme design, implementation, monitoring, reporting and learning. Provide technical support to advocacy teams to track and measure the outcomes and influence of campaigns, policy engagement, and strategic partnerships. Develop and apply methodologies and tools for monitoring policy change, stakeholder influence, and advocacy impact. 3. Accountability and Participation Provide guidance on participatory monitoring approaches, ensuring meaningful inclusion of older people and marginalised groups. Work with programme and network member teams to build inclusive, culturally appropriate feedback and response systems at community or country level. Collaborate with the Data and Accountability Officer to ensure feedback data is analysed and used to inform adaptive programming and advocacy refinement. Promote transparency, responsiveness, and power-sharing through strengthened accountability practices. 4. Organisational Learning and Knowledge Sharing Coordinate learning reviews, after-action reviews, and annual and mid-term reflection processes within and across teams. Document and disseminate key learning, good practices, and innovations. Facilitate cross-organisational learning events, webinars, and communities of practice. 5. Support the development of evaluation terms of reference and methodologies, and support the process, from inception, data collection, analysis and delivery. Coordinate the dissemination of evaluation findings across the organisation, and support teams to use findings to influence strategy, fundraising, and programme design. Capacity Strengthening Design and deliver training and tailored support to HelpAge teams, partners, and network members on MEL and accountability. Develop user-friendly guidance, templates, and toolkits to strengthen MEL practices across the organisation. Build internal capacity for adaptive management and evidence use in decision-making. 7. Planning, Reporting, and Coordination Support the Global Impact Adviser by coordinating key components of HelpAge’s annual business planning, organisational and donor reporting cycles, including coordinating and reviewing inputs from teams across functions and regions. Work closely with the Global Impact Advisor and Data and Accountability Officer to ensure effective data use and alignment of organizational planning and reporting, systems, data use, and frameworks. Actively participate in the relevant cross-team learning and coordination platforms. Contribute MEL insights to fundraising, donor reporting, and strategic planning processes. Skills and experience required Essential Significant experience in Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning in international development, humanitarian, or advocacy-focused organisations. Advanced knowledge of MEAL principles, demonstrated by experience designing M&E frameworks, theories of change, indicators, and MEL plans. Strong technical skills in both quantitative and qualitative data collection and analysis. Experience applying MEL in advocacy, campaigning, or policy-influencing settings. Experience coordinating donor or organisational reporting and translating complex programme and performance information into clear, evidence-based narratives. Experience coordinating organisation-wide or multi-team planning, performance measurement or reporting processes, including setting requirements, managing inputs and challenging incomplete or poor-quality submissions. Knowledge of accountability principles and practical experience with feedback, complaints, and response mechanisms. Strong facilitation skills and experience designing and delivering MEAL training and learning events. Ability to communicate technical information clearly to non-specialist audiences. Proven ability to work collaboratively across diverse teams and cultural contexts. Familiarity with digital data collection and analysis tools (e.g., Power BI, Kobo Toolbox, DHIS2, Excel). Location: Nairobi, Kenya (for exceptional candidates, we are open to other countries where IRW has a country office in the African region) Contract: Permanent Salary: £38,322 Closing Date: 11th October 2026 Islamic Relief Worldwide (IRW) is a faith-based humanitarian and development organisation working to save and transform the lives of some of the world's most vulnerable people. Established in 1984 and operating in over 45 countries, we respond to emergencies, tackle poverty, empower communities, and advocate for lasting change. We are seeking an experienced and strategic Regional Finance Controller - Africa (West and East) to join our Finance & Corporate Services Division. This is a unique opportunity for a senior finance leader who is passionate about financial governance, capacity building, compliance, and driving sustainable improvement across complex international operations. The preferred location for this role is Nairobi, Kenya. However, we recognise that exceptional talent exists across the continent and will consider applications from suitably qualified candidates located within Africa who can support the regional travel requirements and responsibilities of the position. The Finance & Corporate Services Division is a strategic enabler of organisational performance, accountability and sustainability, delivering integrated services across Finance, Treasury, ERP & Digital Transformation, ICT, Supply Chain and Facilities. As part of an ambitious finance transformation programme, the division is strengthening financial governance, independent oversight, service excellence, and data-driven decision making across the organisation's global footprint. About the Role The Regional Finance Controller (RFC) is responsible for providing financial oversight, governance, assurance, compliance, and capacity building across Islamic Relief's country offices and implementing partners throughout West and East Africa. This is far more than a traditional financial control role. You will work closely with Country Directors, Finance Managers, operational teams, and local partners to strengthen financial management practices, build organisational capability, and ensure the highest standards of financial stewardship are embedded across the region. You will play a critical leadership role in improving financial performance, enhancing internal control frameworks, strengthening donor and statutory compliance, and supporting long-term financial sustainability. Through visible, hands-on engagement with country offices and partners, you will help drive a step-change in financial discipline, transparency, accountability, and decision-making. The role combines strategic oversight with practical delivery. You will be responsible for assessing financial performance, mentoring regional finance teams, identifying and mitigating risk, supporting fraud prevention initiatives, and ensuring finance effectively supports programme delivery and donor confidence. Reporting to the Global Finance Operations Lead, you will provide expert technical guidance and leadership across a diverse and complex regional portfolio, supporting the ongoing evolution of Islamic Relief's global finance operating model. The successful candidate will spend approximately 50% of their time travelling across the region, providing direct support to country offices, finance teams, and implementing partners. The Successful Candidate Will Have: A professionally recognised accounting qualification (ACCA, CIMA, ICAEW, ICMA or equivalent). Significant senior-level financial management experience, ideally within the humanitarian, NGO, development, or international non-profit sector. Demonstrable experience leading financial governance, compliance, assurance, and internal control activities across multiple entities or geographical locations. Strong expertise in budgeting, forecasting, financial modelling, financial planning, and scenario analysis. Experience producing consolidated management accounts, variance analysis, financial performance reporting, and strategic financial insight. title: RESPONSABLE DU BUREAU DE PLAIDOYER ET DE LIAISON AUPRÈS DE L’UNION AFRICAINE, Oxfam en Afrique
description:
Type de contrat : Contrat à durée déterminée de 2 ans Grade interne : B1, International Rémunération : conforme à la grille salariale d’Oxfam International. Cette offre comprend les avantages sociaux de base ainsi que les prestations globales applicables au personnel recruté à l’international et relocalisé.Nous considérons que les modalités de travail flexibles sont essentielles pour bâtir le Secrétariat de demain. Nous sommes donc disposés à échanger avec vous sur les modalités susceptibles de vous convenir. Le poste Oxfam en Afrique recherche une personne expérimentée, dotée d’un leadership reconnu et d’un forte capacité d’influence, pour diriger son Bureau de plaidoyer et de liaison auprès de l’Union africaine (UA), basé à Addis-Abeba. En tant que membre de l’Équipe de direction de la Plateforme Afrique, vous piloterez l’engagement d’Oxfam auprès de l’Union africaine et de ses institutions. Vous élaborerez et mettrez en œuvre des stratégies de plaidoyer à fort impact afin d’influencer les politiques et les pratiques à l’échelle continentale. Vous représenterez Oxfam au plus haut niveau auprès de l’UA, nouerez des relations stratégiques et contribuerez à positionner Oxfam comme un partenaire crédible et de confiance. Ce poste joue un rôle central dans la réalisation de la mission d’Oxfam en Afrique : il établit un lien entre les espaces d’élaboration des politiques continentales et les réalités nationales, tout en veillant à ce que les actions de plaidoyer soient cohérentes, porteuses d’impact et ancrées dans les réalités vécues par les communautés. Ce poste relève de la Direction Afrique, avec un rattachement matriciel à la Direction Plaidoyer, Campagnes et Engagement (ACE). Profil recherché Nous recherchons une personne reconnue pour son leadership en matière de plaidoyer et d’influence, disposant d’une solide expérience de collaboration avec l’Union africaine ou des institutions multilatérales comparables. Vous avez démontré votre capacité à concevoir et à mettre en œuvre des stratégies d’influence porteuses d’impact, combinant analyse des politiques, plaidoyer, communication médiatique et partenariats afin de favoriser des changements significatifs. Vous excellez dans l’établissement de relations et la négociation, savez évoluer efficacement dans des environnements complexes associant de multiples parties prenantes et êtes en mesure d’exercer une influence au plus haut niveau. Grâce à votre capacité de réflexion stratégique et d’analyse politique, vous savez traduire les processus de l’UA en possibilités concrètes d’influence et d’impact pour les pays et les partenaires. Votre expérience du leadership vous permet de diriger des équipes diversifiées et de travailler au sein d’un réseau mondial, tout en favorisant la collaboration et la redevabilité. Vous avez une connaissance approfondie du contexte sociopolitique africain et adhérez aux approches féministes, décoloniales et portées par les partenaires. La maîtrise professionnelle de l’anglais et du français est indispensable. Pourquoi nous rejoindre Ce poste offre une occasion rare d’influencer les politiques et les pratiques au plus haut niveau continental. À Oxfam, vous façonnerez notre engagement auprès de l’Union africaine, piloterez le plaidoyer sur des enjeux majeurs tels que les inégalités, la pauvreté et la justice, et collaborerez avec des gouvernements, des diplomates et des institutions internationales pour réaliser des changements concrets. Au sein d’une équipe de direction diversifiée et collaborative, vous contribuerez à rapprocher les politiques continentales des réalités des communautés, afin que les décisions prises au plus haut niveau se traduisent par des résultats tangibles pour les populations partout en Afrique. Ce que nous offrons À Oxfam, nous sommes convaincus que chaque aspect de notre travail peut contribuer à un changement positif. Si vous partagez cette conviction et possédez les compétences nécessaires pour relever les défis liés à ce poste, cette fonction vous offrira de grandes possibilités d’épanouissement personnel ainsi que d’excellentes perspectives d’évolution professionnelle. Oxfam s’engage à proposer une rémunération équitable, sur la base d’une semaine de travail de 36 heures À propos de nous Oxfam est un mouvement mondial de personnes qui agissent ensemble pour mettre fin à l’injustice qu’est la pauvreté. Cela signifie que nous nous attaquons aux inégalités qui maintiennent les populations dans la pauvreté. Ensemble, nous sauvons des vies, protégeons les populations et les aidons à reconstruire leur existence. Lorsqu’une catastrophe survient, nous aidons les personnes à bâtir un avenir meilleur, pour elles-mêmes et pour les autres. Nous agissons sur des enjeux tels que les droits fonciers, le changement climatique et les discriminations à l’égard des femmes. Et nous ne nous arrêterons pas tant que chaque personne sur la planète ne pourra pas vivre à l’abri de la pauvreté. Nous sommes une confédération internationale composée de 22 organisations affiliées et du Secrétariat d’Oxfam International. Avec nos partenaires et les communautés locales, nous menons des actions humanitaires, des programmes de développement et des campagnes dans plus de 76 pays. Oxfam en Afrique (OiA) est une plateforme continentale qui assure la coordination des bureaux pays d’Oxfam en Afrique et collabore avec des organisations de la société civile, des universitaires, des gouvernements et le secteur privé afin de contribuer à une Afrique plus égalitaire, en remettant en cause les structures de pouvoir qui perpétuent les inégalités et les injustices. À cette fin, Oxfam en Afrique apporte un leadership intellectuel dynamique et offre un espace de collaboration à ses partenaires. Oxfam en Afrique joue un rôle moteur dans l’appui aux communautés locales et le renforcement de leur pouvoir d’agir, la promotion de l’égalité de genre, le plaidoyer en faveur de changements de politiques publiques et le renforcement des capacités des organisations locales de la société civile. L’ensemble de notre travail est guidé par nos valeurs fondamentales : Autonomisation, Redevabilité, Inclusion, Courage, Solidarité et Égalité. Notre engagement en matière de safeguarding (Protection contre le harcèlement, l’exploitation et les abus sexuels) Oxfam s’engage à prévenir toute forme de comportement inapproprié au travail, notamment le harcèlement sexuel, l’exploitation et les abus sexuels, les manquements à l’intégrité et les irrégularités financières, ainsi qu’à promouvoir le bien-être des enfants, des jeunes et des adultes. Oxfam attend de l’ensemble de son personnel et de ses volontaires qu’ils partagent cet engagement et respectent notre Code de conduite. Nous accordons une importance primordiale au recrutement de personnes qui partagent nos valeurs et les mettent en pratique. Remarque : Toute offre d’emploi sera subordonnée à la réception de références satisfaisantes et pourra faire l’objet de contrôles appropriés, notamment une vérification du casier judiciaire et des contrôles relatifs au financement du terrorisme. Le Secrétariat d’Oxfam International participe également au Mécanisme interorganisations de divulgation des inconduites (Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme). Conformément à ce dispositif, si une personne candidate a précédemment travaillé pour une autre organisation membre, nous solliciterons auprès de cette organisation des informations concernant toute constatation d’exploitation sexuelle, d’abus sexuels et/ou de harcèlement sexuel survenue pendant son emploi, ainsi que tout incident qui faisait encore l’objet d’une enquête au moment de son départ. En soumettant sa candidature, la personne candidate confirme avoir pris connaissance de cette procédure de recrutement.

How to Apply: **Comment postuler** Si vous souhaitez influencer les politiques continentales et renforcer l’engagement auprès de l’Union africaine afin de favoriser des changements durables en Afrique, nous vous invitons à postuler. Veuillez soumettre un CV à jour et une lettre de motivation via ce lien [https://oxfam.current-vacancies.com/Jobs/Advert/4325897?cid=3360](https://oxfam.current-vacancies.com/Jobs/Advert/4325897?cid=3360) , en démontrant clairement en quoi votre profil répond aux critères essentiels définis dans la fiche de poste de Responsable du Bureau de plaidoyer et de liaison auprès de l’Union africaine. Veuillez noter que seules les personnes présélectionnées seront contactées, généralement dans les deux semaines suivant la date de clôture

Department Network Development Reports to (Line Manager) Director of Global Impact Responsible for (Line managing) Regional Advisers (4) Network SupportLead Humanitarian Capacity Strengthening Manager ( SHAPE ) Network Platform Manager SCORE Programme Manager Indirectly responsible for Country Director – Ukraine (viathe Network Support Lead) Grade F Contract Type Full time equivalent /Open-ended contract About HelpAge HelpAge International works with a diverse global network of around 200 organisations across 99 countries to promote the rights of older people to lead dignified, healthy and secure lives. Through partnership and collaborations, we work to ensure the inclusion of older people across society and strive to deliver a just and fair world for everyone as they get older. Our work is driven by our desire to achieve real impact for older people, to be inclusive, to work in partnership and to learn from our shared experience. As countries prepare for and adapt to population ageing, we are seeking to make a difference at a critical juncture to how societies, economies and institutions adapt to this change. Our Strategy 2030, Ageing in a Just World, sets out how we will work to shape the future we all share. By working together with our partners, we aim to inspire a movement for change. By ensuring all our work promotes older people’s wellbeing, dignity and voice, we seek to transform the lives of older people now and in the future. Guided by our commitment to our values of impact, learning, partnership, and inclusion, we partner with others to bring systemic change and impact at scale. By acting as a supporter, convenor and thought leader, we want to make an impact that matters for older people and their communities. Our organisational culture The culture of the organisation aims to ensure: Accountability for All: Every individual and team member is responsible for their actions and decisions, ensuring alignment with organisational priorities and commitments to partners and network members. Trust, Respect, and Inclusion: We strive to create an environment where mutual trust is the foundation of all relationships, diverse perspectives are valued, and everyone feels included in decision-making processes. Culture of Collaboration: Working together across teams, network members, and partners to share knowledge, maximise impact, and drive collective success, rather than working in silos. Openness and Transparency: Ensuring open communication, clear decision-making processes and actions, and a commitment to sharing information in a way that builds trust and accountability. Collective Responsibilities Within and With Partners and Network: Recognising that achieving our mission requires shared responsibility, we promote joint ownership of decisions, initiatives, and outcomes across HelpAge and its network members and partners. Staff and network members are valued: Staff and network members are recognised, and valued and appreciated for their contributions, fostering an environment where every individual feels respected, supported, and integral to our mission, with their input and expertise recognised as vital to achieving our shared goals. The Behavioural competencies outlined below support this culture. About the Department The Global Impact Team drives HelpAge International’s mission to advance the wellbeing, dignity, and rights of older people, by championing locally led action and global solidarity. At the heart of our work is a thriving, resilient HelpAge global network—a powerful collective of national civil society actors driving change that is rooted in the priorities and experiences of older people. We lead the delivery of HelpAge’s strategic approach to support, convene, and influence, across humanitarian and development contexts, to achieve lasting and inclusive impact. Our goal is to ensure that: Older people have inclusive, improved access to secure and adequate income Older people have safe and secure access to humanitarian assistance Older people have improved access to inclusive health, care, and support services Age-inclusive laws, policies and systems guarantee older people’s rights across all sectors A thriving locally led HelpAge Network drives collective action to uphold older people’s rights, dignity, and wellbeing. About the Job The Head of Network Development will provide strategic leadership for HelpAge International's global network engagement and development, localisation, and capacity strengthening work - advancing our commitment to locally led action and building strong, values-driven relationships with network members and other strategic partners. This role will lead and be accountable for the development and delivery of the HelpAge network strategy, ensuring alignment with our global mission and enabling inclusive, sustainable collaboration across the HelpAge network. The postholder provides strategic leadership for network engagement, development and capacity strengthening across all regions - Africa, Asia, Eurasia and the Middle East, Europe, and Latin America and the Caribbean. They lead through the Regional Advisers rather than delivering regional workstreams personally: setting annual priorities and deliverables for each region, in alignment with organisational priorities, and hold Regional Advisers accountable for delivery through regular performance management and review. This is an evolving role. The postholder ensures the capacity strengthening and localisation offer is shaped by what members themselves identify as their needs and differentiated by region and member segment, rather than applied uniformly. They lead the mechanisms that connect global and regional levels of the network - regional convenings, member-to-member exchange, and the flow of regional intelligence into global strategy, positioning and funding decisions. The role works in close partnership with internal stakeholders - Executive Leadership Group, Board, Leadership Group, and Team Heads - and external stakeholders including network members, civil society organisations, local consortia, donors, and institutional partners. The postholder leads the preparation and quality of Governance Committee submissions and Board papers on network development and engagement. Alongside this regional remit, the role holder will lead directly on coordinating members in the Europe region, and work closely with the Head of Advocacy and Evidencing to develop our strategic niche on donor advocacy in Europe. Key areas for impact/influence and responsibilities To make an impact and influence, the role holder will shape and deliver the HelpAge network strategy and HelpAge's transition to locally led ways of working; provide strategic oversight of network member engagement, localisation, and the organisational capacity sharing strategy; lead HelpAge's support to country transitions, including Ukraine; and build an inclusive, resilient and effective global network of local and national organisations. Network strategy and impact Lead delivery of the HelpAge network strategy, ensuring it supports locally led transitions, strong partnerships and member engagement. Lead the Thriving Network Impact Vehicle (one of six priority areas through which HelpAge delivers its strategy; the other five target external policy change - social pensions, health coverage, humanitarian action, legal rights, climate adaptation - while this one targets the health and sustainability of the network itself) and its results framework, ensuring a clear connection between day-to-day activities and HelpAge's 2030 network targets, and reporting quarterly to the senior leadership team on progress. Lead the preparation and quality assurance of Governance Committee submissions (membership applications, ambassador appointments) and Board papers relating to network development and engagement. Regional leadership Line manage the Regional Advisers. Set annual regional priorities and delivery accountabilities aligned to the network and advocacy strategies, and hold each Regional Adviser accountable for delivery through regular performance management and review. Hold direct responsibility for engagement with Europe-based members, and work with the Head of Advocacy and Evidencing to develop HelpAge's strategic niche on donor advocacy in Europe. Set the strategic frame for network convenings - purpose, frequency, participant profile and hold Regional Advisers accountable for regional and thematic convenings. Chair the strategic reference group INDABA, HelpAge's consultative forum with network members. Membership and capacity sharing Lead and oversee the network membership lifecycle - recruitment, accreditation, due diligence, segmentation and exit - using segmentation to determine how each member is engaged and what level of capacity sharing support they receive, in line with HelpAge's governance frameworks and agreed decision-making authorities. Lead delivery of the Network Capacity Sharing Strategy, translating it into a coherent network-wide offer, integrated across programmes, in collaboration with Programme Support, Advocacy and Evidencing and other relevant teams. Hold the Humanitarian Capacity Strengthening Manager accountable for delivery in priority humanitarian contexts and the SCORE Programme Manager for delivery against SCORE commitments, with both required to feed learning back into the offer; facilitate alignment across different programme approaches and escalate cross-functional issues where appropriate.. Hold the Network Platform Manager 1 accountable for member collaboration platforms that support the network strategy, capacity sharing and member onboarding. Localisation and country transitions Line manage the Network Support Lead. Set the strategic framework for localisation and country transition support and hold them accountable for delivery across relevant country transitions. Ensure network and localisation commitments are reflected in country strategies, programme design and partner engagement, working in collaboration with the Advocacy and Evidencing and Programme Support teams. Resources, Risk Management and Representation Be accountable for achieving the agreed Network Development income target. Working in partnership with the Fundraising & Strategic Partnerships (F&SP) team, play a lead technical and relationship role in shaping fundable propositions, contributing to pipeline development, including ownership of priority donor relationships and the funding pipeline**,** donor cultivation and stewardship, and fundraising for network convening, capacity sharing and the knowledge platform. Act as budget holder for the Network Development portfolio, including grant budgets, with accountability for forecasting, spend against budget, cost recovery and donor compliance. Ensure that organisational standards, policies and frameworks relating to safeguarding, security, fraud and other relevant risks are effectively embedded across Network Development activities, working with the relevant functional leads and holding team leads accountable for compliance within their areas and programmes. Represent HelpAge in global fora on localisation and partnerships, positioning HelpAge as a credible voice on localisation, locally led development, civil society networks, and the role of older people and their organisations - contributing to thought leadership and sector-wide learning. Skills and experience required Essential Proven strategic leadership of a membership network, alliance or partnership portfolio in the international development, humanitarian or civil society sectors, including responsibility for network strategy and its delivery. Demonstrated ability to lead through senior managers - setting the strategic frame, agreeing accountabilities and holding others to delivery - rather than personally owning workstreams. Experience managing diverse, multi-disciplinary and geographically dispersed teams. Extensive experience working with and supporting civil society networks, grassroots organisations and local partners, particularly in low- and middle-income or Global South contexts. Strong knowledge of and commitment to Partner-Led Programming principles, with a proven record of advancing localisation and supporting organisational transitions to locally led ways of working. Experience of the membership lifecycle in a network or alliance - recruitment, accreditation, due diligence and, where necessary, exit. And of segmentation to inform how members are engaged and supported. Track record of income generation against a target, including named ownership of institutional donor relationships and management of a funding pipeline. Budget-holding experience at portfolio level, including grant budgets, forecasting, cost recovery and donor compliance. Experience leading the implementation of a results framework and reporting on progress against strategic targets to an executive or board-level audience. Strong understanding of safeguarding, equity and inclusion, and a demonstrated ability to embed these across teams and partnerships and to hold others accountable for doing so. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build trusted relationships with network members, donors, civil society organisations and institutional actors, and to navigate disagreement between them. Lived experience of the Global South or significant professional experience working in Global South contexts. Desirable Experience designing and delivering a differentiated capacity sharing or capacity strengthening offer across a diverse membership, informed by member-identified need rather than a single global package. Experience of governance processes in a membership body - preparing submissions for a governance committee or board on membership, accreditation or appointments. Experience convening members at regional or global level, including designing convenings for genuine exchange rather than presentation. Familiarity with ageing, inclusion and rights issues in Global South contextsEducation and Qualification Education and Qualifications Degree in international development, public policy, human rights, social sciences, or a related field (or equivalent professional experience). A postgraduate qualification is an asset but not essential where practical experience is strong. Values, Skills, and Ways of Working Ability to work across cultures, sectors, and geographies in inclusive and equitable ways. Excellent communication skills in English (spoken and written); additional languages used in the Global South (e.g., Spanish, French, Arabic) are highly desirable. Deep commitment to locally led development and the principles of Partner-Led Programming. We actively value and encourage candidates with lived experience of inequality, marginalisation, or systemic exclusion—especially related to age, gender, disability, displacement, or economic injustice. Key Behavioural Competencies Working Collaboratively with Others Work collaboratively, building mutual trust and respect, with external organizations and partners to achieve our strategic aims and objectives; being accountable for the work we do together. Adaptability and Flexibility Adapt to new directions or opportunities arising within the organisation and in our work area; being flexible in our role, constantly using the feedback to learn more and evolve further. Supporting and Facilitating Change Lead behavioural and cultural change through embracing a supportive, collaborative and highly inclusive environment where everybody feels supported, respected and engaged. Extend HelpAge’s Reach and Impact Extend HelpAge’s reach and impact by creating and identifying new business development opportunities andbuilding relationships withnew partners. Diversity and Inclusion Lead and promote a culture of including the voices of older people across our support, convening and thoughtleadership roles, in a way that is transformative, empowering and highly inclusive of those marginalised by gender, economic status, disability and other factors of discrimination. Leading Others (for managers) Demonstrate strong leadership to own unit/department and manage people in a well and reputable manner. Create an atmosphere of trust and an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential. Safeguarding HelpAge International is committed to safeguarding the communities with which we work, our partners, staff and any others who we come into contact with. The post holder will also be responsible for: Preventing harm and abuse from our people, operations and programmes to anyone that encounters our work. Reporting all safeguarding incidents you see, hear, hear about or suspect, using our internal reporting mechanism. Complying with all safeguarding framework policies and practices. Completing mandatory training courses relating to our safeguarding policy framework and complying with HR vetting procedures. SAFER RECRUITMENT All employments at HelpAge International will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include misconduct disclosure schemes and terrorism finance checks.

title: Country Representative for Ethiopia, Based in Addis Ababa
description:
WHAT IS IMPACT INITIATIVES ? OUR AIM: IMPACT aims to shape practices and influence policies in humanitarian and development settings, in order to positively impact the lives of people and their communities. Created in 2010, IMPACT is a Geneva-based NGO and the largest independent data provider in contexts of crisis. We aim to support a range of stakeholders in making better, more informed decisions in humanitarian, stabilisation, and development settings. We believe that a key pathway to better planning and decision-making is direct engagement with local communities. HOW DO WE WORK ? IMPACT takes an initiative-based approach to structuring our programming. Each initiative has a specific aim, operational model, and portfolio of solutions. REACH strengthens evidence-based humanitarian decision-making through efficient data collection, management, and analysis - before, during, and after an emergency. PANDA improves the impact of humanitarian and development interventions through programme design, assessments, and monitoring & evaluation. AGORA promotes localised and multi-sectoral aid action in support of the recovery and stabilisation of crisis-affected communities, in partnership with local stakeholders Through our global team of research specialists, on average IMPACT publishes more than 1,700 information products on a yearly basis. In 2010, IMPACT was launched at the initiative of ACTED, an international NGO whose headquarters are based in Paris and is present in thirty countries. The two organizations have a strong complementarity formalized in a global partnership, which particularly allows IMPACT to benefit from ACTED’s operational support in its fields of intervention. We are currently looking for a Country Representative to lead our Ethiopia mission, based in Addis Abeba Position: Country Representative Contract duration: 12 months Location: Addis Abeba, Ethiopia, with potential travel to Kampala, Uganda Starting Date: October / November 2026 Application Deadline: 09 October 2026. COUNTRY PROFILE Since 2018, Ethiopia has experienced escalating insecurity and unrest, including large-scale displacement, loss of life, and widespread destruction of property, following significant domestic political changes. These crises have compounded the effects of recurring climate-related shocks affecting large parts of the country. In November 2020, conflict erupted in the northern Tigray region, triggering significant displacement across Tigray, Amhara, and Afar regions. Since August 2023, renewed conflict in Amhara has further intensified humanitarian needs, leading to the declaration of a state of emergency and restrictions on movement across the region. Together, these crises have severely disrupted livelihoods, constrained access to essential goods and staple commodities, and increased the vulnerability of affected populations, placing additional pressure on humanitarian response capacities across the country. FUNCTIONS Under the management of IMPACT’s Regional Coordinator (RC) for Africa in Geneva, the Country Representative (CR) is responsible for representing IMPACT and managing and developing IMPACT’s programmes in Ethiopia. S/he leads the IMPACT team to achieve program excellence and ensure the highest level of impact and accountability, while ensuring compliance to IMPACT guidelines, policies and standards across the mission. The CR is in regular contact with HQ, ensuring that organizational risks are promptly and clearly communicated to the Regional Coordinator and other relevant HQ Senior Management. S/he will promote organizational vision and core values across the mission and will actively link with HQ to contribute to the implementation of IMPACT’s global strategy. In his/her mission, the Country Representative will be hosted by Acted and will fall under the direct responsibility and management of Acted’s Country Director for all Administrative, Security, Logistics and Finance issues. S/he will therefore fully abide by Acted’s Security, HR, Administration and Logistics rules and regulations, and, in coordination with Acted, will ensure that all IMPACT staff abide by them. RESPONSIBILITIES The Country Representative responsibilities include the following: Strategic Leadership Develop and execute an up-to-date Country Strategy aligned with IMPACT’s global objectives and Ethiopia’s humanitarian landscape. Identify strategic opportunities, consolidate ongoing initiatives, and explore new programme areas to enhance IMPACT’s value to the aid community. Programme and Project Management In coordination with the Deputy Country Representative, oversee programme planning, implementation, and evaluation, ensuring all projects meet objectives, timelines, and compliance standards. Facilitate coordination between IMPACT and partner organizations to achieve efficient project delivery and impact. Fundraising and Donor Engagement Identify and secure funding opportunities in collaboration with HQ and Acted. Lead proposal development and negotiate contracts with donors, ensuring alignment with strategic priorities. Operations Support the Operations Managers and Project Development and Partnership Officers in building and maintaining a broad network of partner organizations to strengthen operational capacity and facilitate the implementation of activities in hard-to-reach and underserved areas. Continue to explore alternative operational models and innovative research approaches to expand geographic and population coverage, particularly among marginalized and difficult-to-reach communities. Ensure regular coordination with Acted's project development and FLATS departments (finance, logistics, administration, transparency, security) at all stages of project development and implementation. Finance and Budget Oversight Manage project budgets and forecast expenses, ensuring accurate and timely financial reporting to HQ and Acted. Mitigate financial risks and ensure optimal budget utilization. Human Resources and Team Leadership In consultation with the Deputy Country Representative, guide and develop the IMPACT team, ensuring performance standards, capacity building, and adherence to IMPACT and Acted’s policies. Coordinate with HQ and Acted for transparent recruitment and career management of staff. External Representation and Coordination Establish and maintain productive relationships with donors, UN agencies, NGOs, and other stakeholders, representing IMPACT’s programmes and strategic interests. Ensure proactive contribution to key humanitarian decision-making forums and promote IMPACT’s programme visibility. Data Protection and Accountability Uphold strict confidentiality of all data collected and engage with communities respectfully, ensuring awareness of programme objectives and methods. REQUIREMENTS Academic qualifications: Excellent academic qualifications, including a Master’s degree in a relevant discipline (International Relations, Political Sciences, Social Research, Development Studies, or similar). Management experience: Previous experience in a senior management role in an INGO at field level. Track record in successful management of international and national teams in humanitarian contexts. Familiarity with aid system: Familiarity with the aid system, and the research community. Communication/reporting skills: Excellent communication and drafting skills for effective reporting, including proven experience in contributing to high level presentations/briefings. Years of work experience: At least 5 years of relevant working experience. Any previous experience in Ethiopia would be an asset. Research skills: Experience in assessments. M&E, field research, evaluations an asset. Multi-tasking skills: Ability to multitask with tight deadlines in complex environment. Level of independence: A self-starter with a proven ability to work independently. Cross-cultural work environment: Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment. Language skills: Fluency in English required**.** Security environment: Ability to operate in a complex and challenging security environment. COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS For this position, salary between 4’050€ and 4’100€ monthly (before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of 500 USD NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in hardship places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere. Accommodation and food provided in ACTED guesthouse Private pension fund, health insurance, and repatriation assistance (& unemployment insurance for EU citizens) This is not a family duty station Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered Contribution to the luggage transportation: between 23kg and 100kg, depending on the length of the contract Annual leave of 36 days per year Predeparture induction - 3 days at IMPACT Initiatives’s HQ in Geneva + one week pre-departure training in ACTED HQ in Paris, including a 4-days in situ security training Tax advice (free 30-minute call with a tax consultant) Enrolment in IMPACT Initiatives Research Foundational Learning Programme within the first 3 months from the start of contract. IMPACT and ACTED prioritize the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees.

title: Ethiopia Senior Tree Expansion Research Officer (Fixed-Term)
description:
About One Acre Fund Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post. In Ethiopia, we engage farmers in agroforestry and community-based seed multiplication to increase farmers’ incomes and make farming systems more resilient. Engaging with local actors at every step but bringing innovative ideas from outside, we are making rural farming more market-friendly and environmentally sustainable. The farmers we work with in Ethiopia have planted more than 30 million trees, produced over 1500 metric tonnes of improved teff seed, and improved the futures of nearly 200,000 community members. Our permanent team numbers over 180 with nearly 1,000 rural seasonal staff supporting them. Our country headquarters are in Addis Ababa and we have a large program office in Bahir Dar, plus several smaller field offices. About the Role The Senior Tree Expansion Research Officer supports the Ethiopia Trees Program's expansion through desk research, primary data gathering, field verification scoutings, and evidence generation to identify and assess potential expansion opportunities across Ethiopia. The role synthesizes geographic, agricultural, environmental, market, and stakeholder information to support strategic expansion decisions and operational readiness. The officer will participate in field scouting visits with the expansion team to validate desk research findings and gather additional insights. Responsibilities Data Collection & Research Conduct desk research to identify and assess potential program expansion areas across regions, zones, and woredas. Collect, analyze, and synthesize agricultural, environmental, demographic, socioeconomic, market, and government data to support expansion planning. Review secondary data from government institutions, research organizations, development partners, and other credible sources to generate evidence-based insights. Monitor demographic, agricultural, environmental, market, and policy trends to identify opportunities and potential risks for program expansion. Develop and maintain databases, trackers, and research documentation to support expansion planning and operational readiness. Verify, clean, and analyze research and field data to ensure quality, accuracy, consistency, and usability. Support the development and continuous improvement of expansion assessment tools, scoring frameworks, research methodologies, and analytical processes. Field & Stakeholder Verification of Data Participate in field scouting and assessment visits to validate desk research findings and collect additional information. Engage with government offices, development partners, local stakeholders, and other relevant actors to verify data, assumptions, and findings. Assess key expansion criteria, including agroforestry suitability, water availability, land suitability, market potential, operational feasibility, scalability, accessibility, and implementation risks. Identify data gaps and discrepancies and coordinate with relevant stakeholders to obtain and validate additional information. Integrate field observations and stakeholder feedback with secondary data to strengthen expansion assessments and recommendations. Reporting & Collaboration Prepare clear and evidence-based assessment reports, analytical summaries, and recommendations to support expansion decisions. Present research findings and recommendations to relevant teams and stakeholders and contribute to expansion planning discussions. Collaborate with the expansion team and relevant technical and operational teams to translate research findings into actionable expansion plans. Maintain clear documentation of research findings, field validation results, assumptions, and recommendations to support decision-making and future reference Reporting, Stakeholder Engagement & Collaboration Support engagement with government institutions, community representatives, development partners, and other relevant stakeholders during expansion assessments and field scouting activities. Coordinate information gathering, stakeholder consultations, and validation activities to support expansion planning and decision-making. Identify collaboration opportunities that strengthen expansion planning, field implementation, and operational readiness. Prepare high-quality assessment reports, presentations, briefing materials, and regular progress updates for internal and external stakeholders. Document research findings, field observations, lessons learned, stakeholder feedback, and key decisions to support knowledge sharing and continuous improvement. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to translate research findings and stakeholder insights into actionable recommendations and expansion plans. Track assigned activities and maintain accurate and up-to-date documentation related to expansion research, assessments, and planning. Perform other research and operational support tasks as assigned to advance the Tree Program’s expansion objectives. Support the recruitment of field staff Career Growth and Development We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career. Qualifications Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for . For this role specifically, you will have: Education Bachelor's degree required. Candidates with academic backgrounds in Forestry, Agroforestry, Agriculture, Natural Resource Management, Environmental Science, Geography, Rural Development, Watershed Management, or related fields are preferred. Experience 2 years or more of relevant professional experience in forestry, agroforestry, agriculture, natural resource management, landscape restoration, rural development, field innovation, government relations, or related fields. Experience conducting research, data collection, expansion assessments, market assessments, or strategic planning. Experience working with government institutions, development partners, or community stakeholders. Experience supporting field assessments or validation exercises is an advantage. Willingness to travel to rural and remote locations for field scouting and stakeholder engagement. Skills Strong analytical, research, and problem-solving skills. Excellent data gathering, analysis, and report writing skills. Ability to synthesize complex information into practical recommendations for decision-making. Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills. Excellent organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines. Ability to useMicrosoft Office, particularly Excel, PowerPoint, and Word. Experience using digital data collection tools is an advantage. Languages Can communicate in English. Fluency in Amharic. Proficiency in Afaan Oromo is preferred Preferred Start Date As soon as possible Job Location Addis Ababa, Ethiopia Benefits Health insurance, paid time off Contract Duration 1 year Eligibility This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Ethiopia.
